scripts.id: CTID - OceanLotus - N/A - Step 0 - Operation Setup
scripts.name: CTID - OceanLotus - N/A - Step 0 - Operation Setup
scripts.description: Executable simulation for documented stage 'Step 0 - Operation Setup'. Source context: This step assumes you have completed the infrastructure setup. Actions completed in this step: - Login to the attacker Kali machine via SSH - Start the control server - Set up attacker terminal windows for execution - Login to the macOS VM on AWS - Required for step 1 At the end of this step the Red Team operator's workspace should be set up to run and manage the emulation. This includes a terminal session providing C2 feedback from the listener and a terminal session to task active implants. Assuming the red team operator is executing Step 1, this also includes establishing a VNC session on macOS in the env.
scripts.command: echo '[START] CTID simulation N/A'; simulation_root=/tmp/morgana-ctid; mkdir -p "$simulation_root"; printf 'host=%s user=%s kernel=%s\n' "$(hostname)" "$(id -un)" "$(uname -sr)" | tee "$simulation_root/readiness.txt"; echo '[SUCCESS] CTID simulation N/A family=readiness'

scripts.id: CTID - OceanLotus - T1016 - Step 1 - Establish Foothold
scripts.name: CTID - OceanLotus - T1016 - Step 1 - Establish Foothold
scripts.description: Executable simulation for documented stage 'Step 1 - Establish Foothold'. Source context: 👋 Handwaving: Assume the user downloaded a Word document from a legitimate, but compromised, site. The Word document (`conkylan.app` - unicorn in Vietnamese) resides in the user's `Downloads` folder. **Step 1** emulates OceanLotus gaining initial access via a malicious file T1204.002 targeting user `hpotter`. Thinking it's a normal Word document, the user, Hope Potter (hpotter), double-clicks `conkylan.app`. (Note: we were not able to disguise the app as a Word document using a homoglyph file extension due to OS updates 🙌 🍎.) The Word document is actually an Application bundle that contains the first stage payload, which does the following: - Removes quarantine flag on files within the application bundle - Installs persistence via LaunchAgent - Extracts and base64 decodes the embedded second stage implant and its communication library component as `/Users/hpotter/Library/WebKit/com.apple
scripts.command: Write-Output '[START] CTID simulation T1016'; $simulationRoot = Join-Path $env:TEMP 'Morgana\CTID'; New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $simulationRoot -Force | Out-Null; $artifactPath = Join-Path $simulationRoot 'CTID-002-t1016.txt'; $childPath = Join-Path $simulationRoot 'ctid-child.ps1'; Set-Content $childPath "Write-Output 'CTID child process telemetry'"; & powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $childPath; Write-Output '[SUCCESS] CTID simulation T1016 family=execution';

scripts.id: CTID - OceanLotus - T1041 - Step 2 - macOS Discovery
scripts.name: CTID - OceanLotus - T1041 - Step 2 - macOS Discovery
scripts.description: Executable simulation for documented stage 'Step 2 - macOS Discovery'. Source context: **Step 2** emulates OceanLotus conducting discovery on a macOS host. OceanLotus enumerates the contents of the `.ssh` folder. Seeing there is an SSH key, the `known_hosts` and `history` files are exfil'ed to the C2 server for analysis. The history file reveals Hope Potter sends files to the file server using SCP. > CTI Note: There is no open-source reporting to support using the `known_hosts` file in > conjunction with local SSH keys 😿. During our research, we did not find reporting > detailing credential collection on macOS. In order to perform lateral movement for the > linux portion of our scenario and staying consistent with using native OS utilities > seen in other reporting, we chose to use `known_hosts` discovery with locally stored > SSH keys.
scripts.command: echo '[START] CTID simulation T1041'; simulation_root=/tmp/morgana-ctid; mkdir -p "$simulation_root"; uname -a; id; ps -eo pid,ppid,user,comm | head -n 12; (ip addr 2>/dev/null || ifconfig 2>/dev/null || true); echo '[SUCCESS] CTID simulation T1041 family=discovery'

scripts.id: CTID - OceanLotus - T1021.004 - Step 3 - Lateral Movement
scripts.name: CTID - OceanLotus - T1021.004 - Step 3 - Lateral Movement
scripts.description: Executable simulation for documented stage 'Step 3 - Lateral Movement'. Source context: **Step 3** emulates OceanLotus transfering tools into the victim enviornment for targeted platforms. OceanLotus downloads Rota Jakiro to the macOS host in the `/Users/hpotter/Library/WebKit` folder (the execution folder for OSX.OceanLotus) as `osx.download`. OSX.OceanLotus then uses SCP to transfer Rota Jakiro to the `\tmp` folder of the Linux host. Using SSH, OSX.OceanLotus changes Rota Jakiro to an executable and executes Rota Jakiro on the Linux host.
scripts.command: echo '[START] CTID simulation T1021.004'; simulation_root=/tmp/morgana-ctid; mkdir -p "$simulation_root"; (timeout 1 sh -c 'echo CTID > /dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/22' 2>/dev/null || true); echo 'loopback remote-service probe completed'; echo '[SUCCESS] CTID simulation T1021.004 family=lateral'

scripts.id: CTID - OceanLotus - T1082 - Step 4 - Discovery on Linux Host
scripts.name: CTID - OceanLotus - T1082 - Step 4 - Discovery on Linux Host
scripts.description: Executable simulation for documented stage 'Step 4 - Discovery on Linux Host'. Source context: **Step 4** emulates OceanLotus executing conducting discovery on the Linux host. For initial collection, Rota Jakiro executes and collects the results from the `uname` syscall. Rota Jakiro sends the following information regarding the Linux host to the C2 server: host name, architecture, and kernel version. Rota Jakiro then downloads and executes a shared object (`mount.so`) to perform discovery for mounted drives connected to the Linux host. The resulting information is saved to `mount.txt`. Rota Jakiro then uploads this file to the C2 server for offline analysis.
scripts.command: echo '[START] CTID simulation T1082'; simulation_root=/tmp/morgana-ctid; mkdir -p "$simulation_root"; uname -a; id; ps -eo pid,ppid,user,comm | head -n 12; (ip addr 2>/dev/null || ifconfig 2>/dev/null || true); echo '[SUCCESS] CTID simulation T1082 family=discovery'

scripts.name: CTID - OceanLotus - T1074.001 - Step 5 - Collection
scripts.description: Executable simulation for documented stage 'Step 5 - Collection'. Source context: **Step five** emulates OceanLotus conducting collection of data using shared objects. OceanLotus downloads and executes a shared object on the Linux host (pdf.so). The shared object performs the following actions: - Creates the `tmp.rota` folder - Starting from the $HOME folder using the `find` command, copy files with a `.pdf` extension into the `tmp.rota` folder - All files are then compressed into a single file named `rota.tar.gz` Rota Jakiro confirms the target file was created. >Note: CTI reporting states Rota Jakiro uses shared objects for code execution. There is >no public CTI reporting documenting exactly what these shared objects are executing. >Therefore, the following code execution is based off general behaviors derived from CTI >reporting targeting linux hosts.
scripts.command: echo '[START] CTID simulation T1074.001'; simulation_root=/tmp/morgana-ctid; mkdir -p "$simulation_root"; mkdir -p "$simulation_root/collection"; printf 'CTID sample data\n' > "$simulation_root/collection/sample.txt"; tar -czf "$simulation_root/collection.tar.gz" -C "$simulation_root" collection; ls -l "$simulation_root/collection.tar.gz"; echo '[SUCCESS] CTID simulation T1074.001 family=collection'

simulation_reasons: The source plan has no machine-readable YAML; documented stages use labeled Morgana-native behavior simulations rather than inferred source commands.

OceanLotus tasks Rota Jakiro to upload the `/tmp/rota.tar.gz` file to the C2 server completing the objective. *Note, the C2 server is limited to recieve data up to but not exceeding 65535 bytes.*
scripts.command: echo '[START] CTID simulation T1041'; simulation_root=/tmp/morgana-ctid; mkdir -p "$simulation_root"; python3 -c "import socket,threading; s=socket.socket(); s.bind(('127.0.0.1',0)); s.listen(1); p=s.getsockname()[1]; threading.Thread(target=lambda: s.accept()[0].recv(64),daemon=True).start(); c=socket.create_connection(('127.0.0.1',p)); c.sendall(b'CTID network simulation'); c.close(); s.close(); print('loopback network telemetry',p)"; echo '[SUCCESS] CTID simulation T1041 family=network'
